proposals.title: Falsifier Declaration required for every completeness claim
proposals.text: Every completeness claim in a plan ('handles X', 'covers states A-E', 'zero behavior change', 'read once AND parsed once', 'pins Z') MUST carry a paired Falsifier Declaration naming (a) the concrete case that would make the claim FALSE and (b) evidence that the case is REACHABLE by the check as written. Reachability is a separate question from assertion strength and is where V4, V5, V6/B2 and B3 lived: unreachable via missing options, via fixture content, via a cast that neutralised the type, and via a baseline captured from the code under test. /qor-audit VETOes any completeness claim lacking one.

proposals.title: Read the COUNT, never the exit code
proposals.text: A truth-checking lint that exits 0 has said one of two different things - 'I checked and it holds' or 'I recognised nothing to check' - and a WARN-only ladder renders them identically. Any verifier whose output carries a coverage count MUST have that count read and compared against the number of items that should have been checked. Zero-items-checked is a FAILURE signal, never a pass.

proposals.title: A tolerance rule may never be keyed on the raw presence of the irregularity it tolerates
proposals.text: NEW from research 2026-08-23. A rule of the form 'tolerate X' where X IS the defect makes the defect self-certifying. Every tolerance MUST be gated on an explicit attestation or a historical cutoff. Upstream exhibit (surfaced, not fixed): ledger_hash.verify() passes the raw _duplicate_previous_hash_members set as tolerated to _report_sequence (ledger_hash.py:543-545), so a duplicate exempts itself; one function away the same file shows the correct shape (_attested_reconciled & _duplicate_previous_hash_members, and find_grandfathered_entries(cutoff=207)). Consumer-side countermeasure: a FailSafe pre-merge CI guard on docs/META_LEDGER.md failing on duplicate entry numbers and on duplicate previous_hash without attestation.

proposals.title: Every declared MUST needs a checker that can fail
proposals.text: qor-substantiate/SKILL.md:382 declares the **Entry ID** line MANDATORY on new ledger entries. It is absent from all twelve entries #585-#596 while Entry #447 carries one - a mitigation that was in use silently lapsed because nothing checks it. A 'MUST' with no falsifier is the same shape as the authoring defect, expressed in doctrine instead of in a test.
